body:
acme-sre: Hey team — after we rotated our client certs yesterday, our service started seeing intermittent 400-level TLS errors when calling Redwood Private endpoints. Worked fine immediately after rotation, then errors started ~30m later.

maria: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error and a quick repro?

acme-sre: Error from our app (nodejs axios): `error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca` and sometimes `certificate verify failed`. Happens on some pods only.

jon: Are you using mutual TLS (client cert) or just server cert rotation?

acme-sre: mTLS — we upload client certs to our side and Redwood requires the leaf cert signed by our internal CA. We rotated the leaf certs using our CA (short-lived 24h), pushed new ones to our pods, and also updated the CA bundle on our side.

kevin: Two common failure modes after rotation: 1) LB / sidecar still has old cert pinned (no hot-reload) 2) OCSP/CRL checks failing because egress to your OCSP responder is blocked. Any envoy/sidecar in front of your app?

acme-sre: Yes we have an envoy sidecar in the pod for inbound/outbound. We didn't restart pods after swapping secrets (we used projected volumes).

maria: Can you run an openssl check from a failing pod and paste output? `openssl s_client -connect <redwood-host>:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -showcerts`

acme-sre: Pasted output below — note the verify error at the end.

-----BEGIN OPENSSL OUTPUT-----
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = AcmeCorp, CN = Acme Root CA
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = AcmeCorp, CN = Acme Intermediate CA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = svc-client.acme.internal
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=svc-client.acme.internal
   i:/C=US/O=AcmeCorp/CN=Acme Intermediate CA
---
SSL handshake has read 3287 bytes and written 512 bytes
---
verify return code: 10 (certificate has expired)
-----END OPENSSL OUTPUT-----

jon: That indicates the client cert we're presenting is being considered expired by the peer. But you said you rotated — double-check the file you mounted into the pod: is it the new leaf cert or still the old one? Projected volume updates do not always update files in-place for processes that read certs once.

acme-sre: Checked — the filesystem shows the new cert content. But the envoy sidecar logs show it loaded the old cert at process start. envoy log: `xds: loaded cert id=abc123 not abc456`

kevin: That matches: envoy isn't automatically hot-reloading that mount. Two remediation paths: 1) restart the envoy sidecars (rolling restart of pods) to pick up new certs, or 2) use SDS (secret discovery service) so envoy pulls updated certs from a control plane. Which do you use?

acme-sre: We're on projected secrets (k8s secret -> volume). We can roll pods but want to understand why only some pods failed.

maria: Might be racey: some pods got restarted by autoscaler during rotation, picked new certs; others kept old envoy process. Also check your CA chain: are you rotating intermediates too? openssl reported \"certificate has expired\" at depth=2 (root) which could be cross-signed expiry.

acme-sre: Oh — we actually rotated the leaf but didn't rotate a cross-signed intermediate that expired last week. Some nodes cached the old chain which included that expired cross-signed intermediate.

jon: That explains intermittent nature. If different pods/sidecars use different CA bundle caches, some verify succeed, others fail. Two fixes: update the CA bundle everywhere (ensure root/intermediate replaced), and do a rolling restart so all sidecars pick the same chain. Also disable OCSP for a quick test if your OCSP responder is unreachable.

acme-sre: We tried temporarily disabling OCSP requests (by setting NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for a quick test) and calls succeeded from a failing pod — suggests OCSP egress blocked + expired cross-signed chain.

kevin: For Redwood Private customers, note that our edge will perform OCSP/OCSP stapling checks if configured; ensure your egress allowlist includes your OCSP responder and any CRL endpoints. Also confirm the CA bundle you uploaded to the console doesn't include the old intermediate.

maria: Action items for us: 1) confirm whether our Private edge saw mixed chains — can someone from infra check the edge cert caching for customer acme-sre? 2) recommend rolling restart for their pods once they replace intermediate. 3) share safe repro steps.

kevin: I'll check logs on our side (looking for `verify error:num=10` and which chain was served). deploy-bot: kicking off `retention-log` search for acme-sre between 1764850000 and 1764860000.

deploy-bot: Started search job #983 — I'll post results when ready. :gear:

acme-sre: Meanwhile we'll swap the intermediate in our CA bundle, restart pods in a canary, and report back. Thanks.

maria: If you want a zero-downtime approach next time: issue new short-lived certs and use SDS or a runtime reloader on envoy, or use a rolling restart staging window. Also consider not rotating intermediate/root without coordinating with Redwood and any pinned chains.

acme-sre: Understood. Will update when can confirm fix. Appreciate the help. :pray:
